environment.note: One cell of the coverage grid (coverage.json): the oxygen bin o2_lt19 and the pressure bin p_lt62_8. The bin edges are the team's choice. No flow range and no gravity level are set. Oxygen bins: 21% with the +/-2.0 point control box (EAWG.atmospheres); 30% is the Moon Base lower bound in the challenge text and the current worst-case test oxygen (CH.moonbase; TB14639.worstcase); 36% is the highest exploration design value, 34% (EA.8.2-34, EAWG.testing), plus the same 2-point box, which is the team's extension. The challenge text gives no upper oxygen bound. Pressure bins: Edges are midpoints between pressures named in the references: 55.2 kPa (8.0 psia), 70.3 kPa (10.2 psia) and 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia) (EAWG.atmospheres, CH.moonbase). needs.reading: A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. Its pressure is not in the table: it is documented for the investigation as a whole (ICES19.pressure, SAF17.pressure), not read per test. needs.note: The counted tests are BASS-II tests (PSI-25) and Saffire-II tests (PSI-99). The Saffire-II table holds one oxygen level near cabin air per test, and a limit cannot be located from one oxygen level. That value is the oxygen the ISS reported when the vehicle departed, about one day before the tests, carried forward from the measured CO2 production (SAF17.o2_initial_II, SAF17.table1_note_i, PSISAF.delay); it is not a sensor reading at ignition. The on-board oxygen sensor traces in the PSI raw data show other levels (PSISAF.o2_traces, read by eye from graphs), and the files do not comment on the difference. A Saffire cell with two numbers gives a value only where a publication names the initial oxygen (sources.json 'documented_start'); no midpoint is computed, and one Saffire-II test has no oxygen value for that reason and is not counted. The Saffire investigators give the flammability-limit objective to Saffire-II alone (SAF16.saffire2, SAF16b.saffire2) and describe the Saffire-I sample as one expected to burn in cabin air (SAF16.saffire1.o2). The BASS-II investigators define an ignition delay from the igniter on and off times and report it against the initial oxygen concentration for PMMA rods (BASS2TM.igndelay). needs.reading: A counted test records the fuel, the oxygen and how the burn ended or an event word. Its pressure is a value of the table (FLEX) or, for BASS-II, a statement of the investigators about the investigation as a whole (ICES19.pressure), not a reading per test. In the FLEX table the ending is extinction, disruption or completion: the count is not a count of extinctions, and 'extinction' is also the recorded end of FLEX tests with no carbon dioxide and no helium added. The indicator 'S1.test_end' gives the count per ending.
needs.note: The one investigation of an extinguishing agent on solid fuels, PSI-26, has an experimental table with sample names only; its link rests on a NASA guide (RG.bass). The investigators' slides report a nitrogen-jet result (BASS13.nitrogen), and no sentence stating an objective was found in them. The counted solid-fuel tests are BASS-II tests with an event word beside the flow settings (extinction, blowoff, no ignition, not sustained); they are also counted for P1 (Flammability limit), because the documents state the oxygen limit under prevention (CP2003.roadmap.limit) and under suppression (CP2004.supp.q3), and counts of different needs must not be added. Every counted test with added carbon dioxide or helium is a FLEX droplet test. The PSI-69 objective names CO2, He and SF6; the FLEX table has no SF6 column. The investigators call the result 'the first extensive data on the stoichiometry and toxicity of combustion products in microgravity' (ICES15.first) and frame the readings as completeness of combustion, stoichiometry and heat release (BASS2TM.products, BASS2TM.sensors), not as detection. needs.reading: A row of this need holds the conditions of a smoke test: material, air flow, aging time and the heating level (a target weight loss rate in the planned SAME matrix, SAMEEIRD.target; the heater resistance ratio Rt/R0 in SAME-R, SAMER.rtr0). needs.note: The PSI experimental tables of SAME (PSI-102) and SAME-R (PSI-101) hold conditions of the smoke tests only. The measured smoke properties (moments of the particle size distribution, mean diameters, smoke detector signals) are reported in the investigators' final reports and papers (SAMEFSR.results, SAME.sizes, SAME.detector) and are not in the tables. The four value rows of the SAME table carry the same values as the planned test matrix of the 2005 requirements document (SAMEEIRD.matrix): they are planned test points, and whether tests were flown at exactly these conditions was not verified. The weight loss rate there is a target value (SAMEEIRD.target): the SAME investigators write that the baseline temperature of each material was selected 'to produce 1 to 2 mg of sample mass loss in 60 sec of heating' (SAME.massloss). The sample mass actually lost was determined by weighing and is not in the table (AST15P.balance). Do not write that the SAME tests were run at 1 or 2 mg/min. In SAME-R the heating level is the heater resistance ratio Rt/R0 (SAMER.rtr0), which is not the sample temperature (SAMER.rtr0.limit). Listing the heating level as useful and not required is the team's choice, although the heating temperature is one of the three controlled parameters (SAME.controls). The SAME table has four more rows that name Kapton, Silicone Rubber, Lampwick and Dibutyl Phthalate with the words 'same conditions as 1-4' and no values; they are not read. The smoke-point rows of PSI-107 (gas jet flames: the fuel flow at which the flame starts to emit soot) are a different kind of smoke condition and are not included.

statements.text: No test in the mapped PSI tables is counted for this need: no test meets every required condition, holds a value for at least one outcome variable of the need and comes from an investigation linked to the need by a supported purpose sentence of the investigators or of a NASA project document.

A row of this need holds the conditions of a smoke test: material, air flow, aging time and the heating level (a target weight loss rate in the planned SAME matrix, SAMEEIRD.target; the heater resistance ratio Rt/R0 in SAME-R, SAMER.rtr0). No row holds a measured smoke property, so no test is counted for this need.

The PSI experimental tables of SAME (PSI-102) and SAME-R (PSI-101) hold conditions of the smoke tests only. The measured smoke properties (moments of the particle size distribution, mean diameters, smoke detector signals) are reported in the investigators' final reports and papers (SAMEFSR.results, SAME.sizes, SAME.detector) and are not in the tables. The four value rows of the SAME table carry the same values as the planned test matrix of the 2005 requirements document (SAMEEIRD.matrix): they are planned test points, and whether tests were flown at exactly these conditions was not verified. The weight loss rate there is a target value (SAMEEIRD.target): the SAME investigators write that the baseline temperature of each material was selected 'to produce 1 to 2 mg of sample mass loss in 60 sec of heating' (SAME.massloss). The sample mass actually lost was determined by weighing and is not in the table (AST15P.balance). Do not write that the SAME tests were run at 1 or 2 mg/min. In SAME-R the heating level is the heater resistance ratio Rt/R0 (SAMER.rtr0), which is not the sample temperature (SAMER.rtr0.limit). Listing the heating level as useful and not required is the team's choice, although the heating temperature is one of the three controlled parameters (SAME.controls). The SAME table has four more rows that name Kapton, Silicone Rubber, Lampwick and Dibutyl Phthalate with the words 'same conditions as 1-4' and no values; they are not read. The smoke-point rows of PSI-107 (gas jet flames: the fuel flow at which the flame starts to emit soot) are a different kind of smoke condition and are not included.
